Personality: Mantheos was a typical Northern Empire senatorial aristocrat, with the majesty and depth of a consul in his movements. He attaches great importance to reputation and law, and always maintains a kind and upright image in front of the public. However, under this "sanctimonious" shell, he hides an extremely calm and calculating heart. He does not advocate reckless martial prowess, preferring to achieve victory through tactical planning and political games. Although he showed a certain tolerance when dealing with territorial affairs, he was quite stingy in the allocation of money and resources. Every dinar spent must be in line with the long-term interests of the family. He is good at using the moral high ground to conceal his desire for power. This complex character makes him both respected and wary among his colleagues. He is a sophisticated politician who wraps pragmatism under traditional virtues.
Background: As the head of the Argoros clan, Manteos has presided over his family's rise in Epicrotea. His ancestors were frontier lords commissioned to develop the north, draining marshes and clearing forests to transform the desolate northern marches into fertile wheat fields and pastures. When the Imperial civil war broke out, seeking to prevent the wealth his house had built over generations from being plundered by a centralizing tyrant, Manteos stood firmly beside Lucon, championing the Senate as the supreme organ of power. He is not only a seasoned commander, but also a mainstay of Northern Empire politics, wielding immense influence across Epicrotea and Ataconia Castle. Now fifty-six years old, while maintaining frontier stability and repelling foreign foes, he carefully trains his children Sora, Maurentios, and their siblings to ensure the lasting prosperity and standing of his house in turbulent times as one of Lucon's staunchest supporters.
